headline: Broad-based demand lifts revenue, margins, and profit
summary_short: NXP's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 19% y/y to $3.50 billion, with GAAP operating income up 56% y/y to $1,071 million and GAAP diluted EPS of $3.02, up 72% y/y.
summary_long: Revenue grew across all four end markets and regions, led by Industrial & IoT (+38% y/y) and Communications Infrastructure (+41% y/y), with management citing strength in Software-Defined Vehicles, Physical AI, and an emerging Data Center growth driver. GAAP operating margin expanded to 30.6% as revenue growth outpaced a 6% rise in operating expenses. Sequential GAAP operating income fell 29% only because Q1 2026 included a one-time $621 million gain on the sale of a business line; excluding that, underlying operating performance improved q/q. NXP guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to $3.65-3.85 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $3.89-$4.32. Cash fell to $3.22 billion after a $750 million note repayment and $360 million of capital returned to shareholders.

drivers.explanation: Management cited growth across all end markets and regions, driven particularly by Software-Defined Vehicles and Physical AI, with Data Center emerging as an additional growth engine.
Y/y margin expansion (GAAP operating margin 30.6% vs 23.5%) is consistent with revenue growth (+19%) outpacing the ~6% rise in combined R&D and SG&A expense.

The 29% q/q drop in GAAP operating income is not a deterioration: Q1 2026 included a one-time ~$621 million gain on sale of a business (the reconciliation's 'Other incidentals'), which non-GAAP operating income excludes.
EPS growth tracks GAAP net income growth almost one-for-one, since diluted share count was essentially flat y/y (254.0M vs 253.8M).
